cues.en: 21 grams.
That is the mass of all of the electrons in your body. If like me, you weigh about seventy kilograms.
cues.zh: 这就是你体内所有电子的质量。如果你像我一样，体重大约七十公斤。

cues.en: Now all of that mass comes from the Higgs mechanism,
cues.zh: 所有这些质量都来自希格斯机制，

cues.en: which means that as your electrons are traveling through space time they interact with the Higgs field and it's that that gives them their mass. It slows them down and stops them from traveling at the speed of light.
cues.zh: 这意味着当你的电子在时空中穿行时，它们会与希格斯场相互作用，正是这种相互作用赋予了它们质量。它使它们减速，阻止它们以光速运动。

cues.en: But most of your mass doesn't come from the Higgs mechanism
cues.zh: 但你大部分的质量并不来自希格斯机制

cues.en: and neither does all of the stuff that you see around you.
cues.zh: 你周围看到的所有东西也是如此。

cues.en: The mass is coming from somewhere quite different and that's because most of your mass and most of this mass comes from neutrons and protons and they're not fundamental particles. They're made of constituent particles called quarks. Now, the theory that describes quarks and their interactions with each other through gluons is called quantum chromodynamics,
cues.zh: 质量来自一个完全不同的地方，这是因为你大部分的质量以及这里大部分的质量都来自中子和质子，而它们不是基本粒子。它们由称为夸克的组成粒子构成。描述夸克及其通过胶子相互相互作用的理论叫做量子色动力学，

cues.en: and chromo is the Greek word for color.
cues.zh: 而chromo是希腊语中颜色的意思。

cues.en: So in some way, these objects are meant to carry the color charge.
cues.zh: 所以在某种程度上，这些物体被认为携带色荷。

cues.en: But they are much much smaller than the wavelength of visible light, so there is no way that they are actually colored. But it's a useful analogy that helps us think about how they interact and the particles that they can make up. Now the rules are pretty simple. In order for a particle to exist, it must be colorless or white like this house. Now you can accomplish that in two different ways.
cues.zh: 但它们比可见光的波长小得多得多，所以它们实际上不可能有颜色。但这是一个有用的类比，帮助我们思考它们如何相互作用以及它们能构成哪些粒子。规则很简单。一个粒子要存在，它必须是无色的或白色的，就像这座房子一样。你可以通过两种不同的方式做到这一点。

cues.en: You could make three quarks where each one is a different color, red, green, and blue, so overall they combine to produce white.
cues.zh: 你可以让三个夸克各带一种不同色荷——红、绿、蓝，这样它们合起来就产生白色。

cues.en: Or you could use a quark and an anti quark,
cues.zh: 或者你也可以用一个夸克和一个反夸克，

cues.en: where one is a color like green and the other is its
cues.zh: 其中一个是像绿色这样的色荷，另一个是它的

cues.en: anti color, say magenta.
cues.zh: 反色，比如品红色。

cues.en: Now what I'd like to do on this little patch of beach behind me is simulate how quarks actually bind together and form different particles.
cues.zh: 现在，我想在我身后这一小片沙滩上，模拟夸克实际如何束缚在一起、形成不同粒子。

cues.en: Now, for this you need to remember that in the last video we talked about how empty space is not truly empty. So the beach here has these undulations in it which represent fluctuations in the gluon field. But you have to imagine this beach sort of rippling and these bumps coming and going. Now that's really important because to get rid of those fluctuations actually takes energy.
cues.zh: 现在你需要记住，上个视频我们讲过，空无一物的空间并非真正空无一物。所以这里的沙滩有这些起伏，代表胶子场中的涨落。但你要想象这片沙滩在微微波动，这些隆起不断出现又消失。这一点很重要，因为消除这些涨落实际上需要能量。

cues.en: And this is an important part of binding the quarks together.
cues.zh: 而这是把夸克束缚在一起的重要一环。

cues.en: The existence of quarks actually suppresses the gluon fluctuations
cues.zh: 夸克的存在实际上会抑制胶子涨落，

cues.en: and creates what's called a flux tube, an area where there is really nothing in the vacuum and that's in between this quark and the antiquark and that pairs them up and creates what's called a meson, the quark antiquark pair. What's interesting about the flux tube is that as these quarks become more separated,
cues.zh: 并产生所谓的通量管，也就是真空中真正空无一物的区域，它位于这个夸克和反夸克之间，把它们配成对，形成所谓的介子，即夸克-反夸克对。通量管有趣的地方在于，当这些夸克分得越来越开时，

cues.en: the flux tube remains the same diameter and the same sort of depth of suppression of the field, which means that the force doesn't actually increase. It's not like a spring, it's not like an elastic band. The force is the same that is pulling these quarks back together.
cues.zh: 通量管仍保持相同直径，场被抑制的程度也大致相同，这意味着力实际上并没有增大。它不像弹簧，也不像橡皮筋。把它们拉回一起的力始终相同。

cues.en: But you are putting more work in as you move these quarks and any quarks further apart.
cues.zh: 但当你把这些夸克以及任意夸克分得越远，你投入的功就越多。

cues.en: And so for a time people thought, well these quarks are always going to be confined however far you move them, you're just going to get a really long flux tube. But what actually happens is that you put in enough energy that you can actually create
cues.zh: 于是有一段时间，人们以为，这些夸克无论你移得多远都会被禁闭，你只会得到一根非常长的通量管。但实际发生的是，你注入足够能量后，真的可以创造出

cues.en: a quark anti quark pair. Nevertheless,
cues.zh: 一对夸克-反夸克。不过，

cues.en: the quarks are still confined. You can never see an individual quark
cues.zh: 夸克仍然被禁闭。你永远看不到单个夸克

cues.en: because if you try to pull it out, you put so much energy into the situation that another quark antiquark pair will be created. Now to form a proton, we're gonna need an up quark, another up quark,
cues.zh: 因为如果你试图把它拉出来，你会给这个情形注入太多能量，以至于会产生另一个夸克-反夸克对。现在要形成一个质子，我们需要一个上夸克、另一个上夸克，

cues.en: and a down quark.
cues.zh: 以及一个下夸克。

cues.en: Now the standard model of a proton that you've probably seen involves these quarks bounded together by little gluon springs that go between them. We know that that picture is totally wrong now.
cues.zh: 你可能见过的质子标准模型，是这些夸克由它们之间的小胶子弹簧束缚在一起。我们知道那幅图景现在完全错了。

cues.en: Even in the best sense you might have hoped that you would see flux tubes around the edge of the triangle, but, we know that in fact they don't do that. That you get these y shaped flux tubes.
cues.zh: 即便往最好处想，你也许希望会看到三角形边缘周围的通量管，但我们知道实际上它们不是那样。你会得到这些 Y 形通量管。

cues.en: The crazy thing about a proton is that there may be more than three quarks there.
cues.zh: 质子最疯狂的地方在于，那里可能不止三个夸克。

cues.en: You see, you can have additional quark anti quark pairs pop in and out of existence. So at any given time, there could be five or seven or nine, any odd number of quarks could make up the proton.
cues.zh: 你看，额外的夸克-反夸克对可以不断出现又消失。所以在任意时刻，可能有五个、七个或九个，任意奇数个夸克都可能组成质子。

cues.en: So this is what a proton actually looks like. You can see that the quarks like to sit on those lumps in the gluon field. And you can see the two up quarks and a down quark, but there's also a strange quark and an anti strange quark,
cues.zh: 这就是质子实际的样子。可以看到夸克喜欢待在胶子场中的那些团块上。你能看到两个上夸克和一个下夸克，但还有一个奇异夸克和一个反奇异夸克，

cues.en: which is strange because you don't normally think of these quarks being inside a proton, but they can be at any particular point in time. You can also see that these quarks have cleared out the vacuum,
cues.zh: 这很奇怪，因为你通常不会想到这些夸克存在于质子内部，但它们可以在任何特定时刻出现。你还可以看到这些夸克清空了真空，

cues.en: and you can see there's kind of these flux tubes,
cues.zh: 你能看到这些通量管，

cues.en: which are the areas where the gluon field has been suppressed.
cues.zh: 也就是胶子场被抑制的区域。

cues.en: And that's really what's binding these quarks together. That's the strong force that binds quarks
cues.zh: 这才是真正把夸克束缚在一起的东西。这就是强相互作用力，把夸克束缚

cues.en: into the heart of the proton. It is intrinsically related to the fact that clearing out those fluctuations has more energy than
cues.zh: 在质子核心。它本质上与这样一个事实相关：清空那些涨落所需的能量比

cues.en: where they are. That's right. It costs energy to clear the vacuum up. So
cues.zh: 它们所在之处更多。没错。清空真空需要消耗能量。那么

cues.en: where is the mass of the proton really coming from? Well, of course the constituent quarks do interact with the Higgs field and that gives them a small amount of mass. But if you add up the mass of all the quarks in the proton, it would only account for about 1%
cues.zh: 质子的质量到底来自哪里？当然，组分夸克确实与希格斯场相互作用，这给它们带来少量质量。但如果把质子中所有夸克的质量加起来，也只占其总质量的约1%

cues.en: of its total mass.
cues.zh: 占其总质量。

cues.en: So where's the rest of the mass coming from? The answer is energy.
cues.zh: 那么其余的质量来自哪里？答案是能量。

cues.en: You know Einstein's famous equation e equals m c squared. Well, says we got a lot of energy for just a little bit of mass.
cues.zh: 你知道爱因斯坦著名的方程E=mc²。它说的是，一点点质量就对应着巨大的能量。

cues.en: But if you rearrange the equation, you can see that we can get an amount of mass if there is lots of energy there. And that is really where most of the mass, the proton is coming from. It's from the fact that there are these energy fluctuations in the gluon field and the quarks are interacting with those gluons.
cues.zh: 但如果你重新排列这个方程，你会发现只要有大量能量，就能得到一定的质量。而这正是质子大部分质量的来源。它源于胶子场中存在这些能量涨落，而夸克与这些胶子相互作用。

cues.en: That is where your mass is coming from. It's coming from the energy that's in there. You know Einstein talked about, well if I had a hot cup of tea, it would actually have a slightly greater mass than the same cup of tea when cold.
cues.zh: 你的质量就来源于此。它来自那里的能量。你知道爱因斯坦说过，如果我有一杯热茶，它的质量实际上会比同样一杯冷茶略大一些。

cues.en: And he was right. I mean you can't measure it with a cup of tea, but most of your mass you owe to e equals m c squared. You owe to the fact that your mass is packed with energy because of the interactions between the quarks and these gluon fluctuations in that gluon field. I think it's extraordinary because what we think of as ordinarily empty space, know, that turns out to be the thing that gives us all most of our mass.
cues.zh: 他说得对。我是说，你没法用一杯茶测量出来，但你大部分的质量都要归功于E=mc²。归功于这样一个事实：由于夸克与胶子场中那些胶子涨落之间的相互作用，你的质量充满了能量。我觉得这非常不可思议，因为我们通常认为是空旷的空间，结果却正是赋予我们大部分质量的东西。
